title: Comparatives 1: The One-Word Form (stem + ее)
titleRussian: Сравнительная степень 1: Форма в одно слово (основа + ее)
description: Russian builds 'newer, prettier, more interesting' by adding -ее to the adjective stem. The result is one word that never changes for gender or number.
descriptionRussian: Русские формы вроде «новее», «красивее», «интереснее» образуются прибавлением -ее к основе прилагательного. Это одно слово, и оно не меняется по роду и числу.
intro: Russian gives you a comparative that never changes. One form covers every gender and both numbers, which after two books of declension tables should feel like a holiday. The catch is where it can stand: this form works after a subject or after a verb, but it cannot sit in front of a noun. That job needs a different construction, and it waits until lesson 7.
rules: To build the one-word comparative, drop the adjective ending and add -ее: новый → новее, холодный → холоднее, интересный → интереснее.
This comparative never changes. One form covers every gender and both numbers: дом новее, машина новее, телефоны новее.
It goes after the subject (Дом новее) or after a verb as an adverb (Антон поёт красивее). It cannot stand in front of a noun the way a normal adjective does.
Never add более in front of this -ее form, and never add a gender or plural ending after it. The suffix alone does the whole job.
examples: Этот дом новее. (This house is newer.) After the subject; новее does not change.
Сегодня холоднее, чем вчера. (Today is colder than yesterday.) холоднее stays the same; чем = than.
Эта книга интереснее. (This book is more interesting.) After the subject.
Дети сегодня веселее. (The children are happier today.) Plural subject, but веселее does not add a plural ending.
Антон работает быстрее. (Anton works faster.) After the verb, as an adverb.
Молоко полезнее, чем сок. (Milk is healthier than juice.) полезнее from полезный (useful, healthy).

items.promptEnglish: This house is newer than that one.
items.hint: Drop the ending of новый and add -ее.
items.explanation: Новее is the one-word comparative of новый: stem нов- + -ее. It never changes, so it does not agree with дом.

items.hint: You need 'colder', not 'cold'. Add -ее to the stem.
items.explanation: Холоднее is the one-word comparative of холодный: stem холодн- + -ее.

items.promptEnglish: The children are happier today than yesterday.
items.hint: The subject is plural, but does the comparative add a plural ending?
items.explanation: Веселее is the comparative of весёлый, and it does not change for the plural subject дети. That is the key point: the one-word comparative is the same for everyone.

items.promptEnglish: This book is more interesting than the film.
items.hint: Drop the ending of интересный and add -ее.
items.explanation: Интереснее is the comparative of интересный: stem интересн- + -ее. The same form works for any subject: книга, фильм, дети.

items.hint: This describes the verb 'works'. The comparative also works as an adverb.
items.explanation: Быстрее is the comparative form, used here after the verb работает as an adverb ('works faster'). The one-word comparative does double duty: after a subject (Антон быстрее) and after a verb (работает быстрее).

items.promptEnglish: Health is more important than money.
items.hint: The subject здоровье is neuter, but the comparative still does not change.
items.explanation: Важнее is the comparative of важный: stem важн- + -ее. Even though здоровье is neuter, the comparative does not add a neuter ending, because it never changes.

blanks: Весной _____ , чем зимой. (In spring it is warmer than in winter.)
Эта дорога _____ , чем та. (This road is more beautiful than that one.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both blanks need the one-word comparative. Теплее = warmer (from тёплый), красивее = more beautiful (from красивый). Neither changes for gender or number: теплее works with weather, красивее works with дорога (feminine).

errorCorrection.sentence: Эта комната более светлее, чем кухня.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This room is brighter than the kitchen.
errorCorrection.explanation: The suffix -ее already means 'more', so светлее = 'brighter'. Putting более ('more') in front of it doubles up, like saying 'more brighter' in English. Use the suffix alone: светлее.

errorCorrection.sentence: Сегодня погода теплее, и небо стало светлая.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The weather is warmer today, and the sky has become brighter.
errorCorrection.explanation: The sentence says the sky 'became brighter', so it needs the comparative светлее, matching теплее just before it. Светлая is the plain adjective ('bright', feminine), which states a quality but not an increase.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The new phone is more beautiful than the old one.
errorCorrection.explanation: The word чем ('than') signals a comparison, so you need 'more beautiful': красивее. Красивый is just the plain adjective ('beautiful'), which cannot make a comparison.

errorCorrection.sentence: Эти парки красивее, и этот парк тоже красивейший.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These parks are more beautiful, and this park is also more beautiful.
errorCorrection.explanation: The sentence makes a simple comparison ('also more beautiful'), so it needs красивее, which stays the same for singular and plural alike. Красивейший is a 'most beautiful' superlative, a stronger claim than the sentence makes.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This book is more interesting than the film.
minimalPairs.explanation: The English 'more interesting' needs the comparative интереснее. Интересная is just the plain adjective ('interesting', feminine), which states a quality but does not compare.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: These houses are newer than those.
minimalPairs.explanation: The subject дома is plural, but the comparative новее does not add a plural ending: it never changes. Новые is the plain plural adjective ('new'), which does not mean 'newer'.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each form: is it a one-word comparative ('more X'), or just the plain adjective ('X')?

sentenceBuilding.hint: Subject first, then the one-word comparative новее (it does not change).

sentenceBuilding.translation: This book is more interesting than the film.
sentenceBuilding.hint: интереснее stays the same. Build: subject, comparative, чем, the thing compared.
The subject дети is plural, but веселее does not get a plural ending.

reviewVocab.definition: newer (the one-word comparative of новый; it never changes for gender or number)
colder / warmer (one-word comparatives of холодный and тёплый, common for weather; built with -ее)
reviewVocab.example: Сегодня холоднее, чем вчера, но завтра будет теплее.

reviewVocab.definition: more interesting (the one-word comparative of интересный; the same form for any subject, singular or plural)
